title: Big Moments with the Crash
description: Use the crash cymbal to mark the start of a new section and make it land with weight.

steps.title: What the crash is for
steps.description: The crash is the loudest thing on the kit, so drummers use it sparingly. You'll hear it on the first beat of a chorus, at the end of a fill, or when the band hits something together. It's like an announcement: "new part starts here". Hit it too often and it stops meaning anything.

steps.title: Hit the crash
steps.description: Hit the crash and listen to it bloom and fade out.
steps.hint: The yellow pad on the bottom row, labelled CRS. It's second from the right.

steps.title: Crash with the kick
steps.description: Hit the crash and kick together. This is the go-to move on beat 1 of a new section. The kick gives the crash weight.
steps.hint: KCK is top left and CRS is on the bottom row. Hit them as close together as you can.

steps.title: Add the snare
steps.description: Now crash, kick and snare all at once. Save this one for the biggest moments in a song, like the last chorus.
steps.hint: Kick and snare sit side by side at the top left. Add the crash from the bottom row.

steps.title: Crash and ride
steps.description: Hit the crash and ride together. Two cymbals at once gives you a wash, a big wall of shimmer. It's nice at the end of a song or for a dramatic swell.
steps.hint: They're neighbours at the right end of the bottom row: CRS, then RDE.

steps.title: When to crash
steps.description: When will you most often hear a drummer hit the crash?

quizOptions.label: At the start of a new section
Only at the very end of a song
